title: AI doesn't read words. It reads tokens.
description: Language models split text into tokens, not words. Here's what a token is and why it explains length limits.

scenes.say: AI doesn't read words the way you do. It reads tokens, and that explains a lot about its limits.
A token is a piece of a word. In English, it's roughly four characters.
Before a model reads anything, your text is split into tokens. Each token is converted into numbers, and the model works on those numbers. Then its output is turned back into text.
That's why the counts differ. A common short word is often a single token. Rarer or longer words can be split into several pieces.

A rule of thumb: a hundred tokens is about seventy-five English words. Length limits count tokens, and your prompt and the reply share that space. So a long prompt leaves less room for the answer. Share this with anyone who's hit a length limit.
